query_text: what temperature can food be accepted at

action.query: FDA Food Code receiving food temperature cold TCS food 41°F hot food 135°F eggs milk shellfish
queries: FDA Food Code receiving food temperature cold TCS food 41°F hot food 135°F eggs milk shellfish

annotations.title: Wash. Admin. Code § 246-215-03235 - Specifications for receiving-Temperature (FDA Food Code 3-202.11) | State Regulations | US Law | LII / Legal Information Institute

content.text:
Food should generally be **accepted/received at these temperatures**:

- **Cold TCS foods**: **41°F or below** / **5°C or below**
- **Hot TCS foods**: **135°F or above** / **57°C or above**
- **Frozen foods**: Must be **frozen solid** with no signs of thawing/refreezing
- **Shell eggs**: Usually **45°F or below** / **7°C or below**
- **Milk and shellfish**: May have specific legal receiving temperatures, but should be cooled to **41°F or below** after receiving

If food is in the **temperature danger zone** — between **41°F and 135°F** — it should usually be **rejected**, unless a specific rule allows otherwise. ([law.cornell.edu](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/washington/WAC-246-215-03235?utm_source=openai))
